summary: Host archive preserves exact received bytes with fsync and receive times, separate ordinal/boot-ID records including repeated IDs, explicit sequence/loss/bound errors, exclusive paths and SHA-256 manifests. Nine real pipe/subprocess host controls pass, including killed collector and 80 boots under a 32-FD limit. Shared make check passed 210 tests. No phone execution or qualified transport claimed.
acceptance_assessment: Existing output paths are refused without mutation. New boot markers use distinct host ordinals even when producer IDs repeat; reuse is flagged.
Raw bytes precede parsing/fsync. Fragmented, invalid, oversize and truncated data remain in received.bin; gaps/drop/timeout/size/interruption prevent a clean verdict.
Crash test retains fsynced raw bytes with no success manifest; restarting the collector uses another directory.
Final tests-004 and demo-002 match committed collector behavior; earlier test/demo runs are retained, not overwritten.
limitations: Synthetic producers and host controls only. Native producer/physical early-log transport not implemented or qualified.
Complete received stream is not complete hardware execution or successful iOS boot.
NAT-017 remains pending: board-specific channel and canary/reset retention need qualification and a new image-specific decision. Current Android was not rebooted or flashed.
Time and byte bounds stop collection explicitly; bytes never received or made durable cannot be guaranteed.
